title: I Printed the Wine-Tasting Spit-Bucket Policy for the Host Who Refilled

parts.text: I paid a five-pour flight at 3:20 p.m. and the host refilled his own glass from the spit bucket's reserved bottle. The tasting policy on the menu said: HOST POURS MEASURED. NO PERSONAL REFILLS FROM FLIGHT BOTTLES. I was thirty, designated taster, holding a pour that already looked short. Host Gia said, "Palate calibration." I pointed at the menu. She poured again. "Calibration is the house." I photographed the extra pour, the menu, and my short glass. Then I printed the menu policy at the till and asked the tasting room manager to measure both glasses. At 3:26 the manager asked why Gia's name was on a refill ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The manager can see a host refill against the measured-pour menu Gia used.

social.video_title: The host refilled from the flight bottle — Part 1/2
social.description: Short glass, palate calibration, and a menu rule. I asked for a measure. Would you have pretended it was oak?

parts.text: Gia called it a rinse until the measure showed my pour two ounces light. I kept the ticket, the menu, and the photo. They reset the flight. Gia told the barrel the menu was always about optics. Optics is a word hosts use when a cylinder exists. Pour policy now has a second line: CALIBRATION BUYS A GLASS. I taste even. Gia spits like a guest. The bucket finally has only spit.

social.description: Refill ticket, a reset flight, and a second line on the menu. Was a rinse ever two ounces?
